# Ezekiel 4 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** "And-you, son-of man, take for-yourself a-brick and-put-it before-you, and-engrave upon-it a-city — Jerusalem.

**2** And-lay siege against-it, and-build against-it a-siege-wall, and-heap-up against-it a-ramp, and-set against-it camps, and-place against-it battering-rams all-around.

**3** And-you, take for-yourself an-iron griddle, and-set-it [as] an-iron wall between-you and-between the-city, and-set your-face against-it, and-it-shall-be under-siege, and-you-shall-besiege-it — a-sign it [is] for-the-house-of Israel.

**4** And-lie upon your-left side, and-put [the]-iniquity-of the-house-of Israel upon-it; [the]-number-of the-days which you-lie upon-it, you-shall-bear their-iniquity.

**5** And-I — I-have-appointed to-you the-years-of their-iniquity [by the]-number-of days: three-hundred and-ninety days; and-you-shall-bear [the]-iniquity-of the-house-of Israel.

**6** And-you-shall-complete these, and-you-shall-lie upon your-right side a-second-time, and-you-shall-bear [the]-iniquity-of the-house-of Judah forty days — a-day for-a-year, a-day for-a-year, I-have-appointed-it for-you.

**7** And-to the-siege-of Jerusalem you-shall-set your-face, and-your-arm [shall be] bared, and-you-shall-prophesy against-it.

**8** And-behold, I-have-put upon-you ropes, and-you-shall-not-turn from-your-side to-your-[other]-side until you-complete the-days-of your-siege.

**9** And-you, take for-yourself wheat and-barley and-beans and-lentils and-millet and-spelt, and-put-them in-one vessel, and-make them for-yourself [into]-bread; [the]-number-of the-days which you [are]-lying upon your-side — three-hundred and-ninety days — you-shall-eat-it.

**10** And-your-food which you-eat [shall be] by-weight — twenty shekels per-day; from-time to-time you-shall-eat-it.

**11** And-water by-measure you-shall-drink — a-sixth-of a-hin; from-time to-time you-shall-drink.

**12** And-[as]-a-cake-of barley you-shall-eat-it, and-it — upon dung-of [the]-excrement-of man you-shall-bake-it before-their-eyes."

**13** And-YHWH said, "Thus shall-eat the-sons-of Israel their-bread unclean among-the-nations where I-will-drive-them."

**14** And-I-said, "Ah, Lord YHWH! Behold, my-soul has-not-been defiled, and-a-carcass and-a-torn-thing I-have-not-eaten from-my-youth until now, and-there-has-not-come into-my-mouth flesh-of uncleanness."

**15** And-He-said to-me, "See, I-have-given to-you [the]-dung-of cattle in-place-of [the]-dung-of man, and-you-shall-make your-bread upon-it."

**16** And-He-said to-me, "Son-of man, behold-Me breaking [the]-staff-of bread in-Jerusalem, and-they-shall-eat bread by-weight and-in-anxiety, and-water by-measure and-in-horror they-shall-drink,

**17** so-that they-lack bread and-water, and-they-shall-be-appalled each-one and-his-brother, and-they-shall-waste-away in-their-iniquity.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **4:1-3**: The brick-engraving and iron griddle create a prophetic tableau — a miniature siege model. The iron wall between prophet and city symbolizes YHWH's separation from Jerusalem.

- **4:5-6**: 390 days for Israel, 40 for Judah. The LXX reads 190 for Israel. The day-for-a-year principle (yom la-shanah) creates a symbolic chronology of sin.

- **4:14**: Ezekiel's protest echoes priestly purity concerns (Lev 11, 17:15). Unlike Jeremiah's objections, Ezekiel's is cultic — he guards his ritual cleanness even in exile.

— EMET
